title: Band-Pass Filter - Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD) for Public Safety Band Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Stefan Richter

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Band-Pass Filter filter targeting Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD) for Public Safety Band Filter. The filter is designed on 36° YX LiTaO3 substrate with a target center frequency of 3970.9 MHz and bandwidth of 61.8 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the Public Safety Band Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Band-Pass Filter
- Frequency Band: Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD)
- Application: Public Safety Band Filter
- Substrate: 36° YX LiTaO3
- Package: QFN (Quad Flat No-Lead)
- Design Tool: Cadence AWR Microwave Office
- Design Center: San Jose Advanced Design Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the Band-Pass Filter design targeting Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       3970.9 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       61.8 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.9 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 23.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 33.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 38.0 dB
Q Factor:               11266
Temperature Coefficient:-11.1 ppm/°C
Die Size:               1.5 x 1.8 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   9
Electrode Material:     Mo
Passivation:            Si3N4
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Cadence AWR Microwave Office and load the Band-Pass Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: 36° YX LiTaO3 with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 3970.9 MHz, BW 61.8 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.9 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (QFN (Quad Flat No-Lead)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, 36° YX LiTaO3).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Keysight N5227B PNA.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 11913 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.9 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 23.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 93 MHz offset >= 33.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 5 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 5.5 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +31 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 500 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 91%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-02-13
Devices Tested:         90
Insertion Loss (meas):  2.57 dB
Return Loss (meas):     24.9 dB
Rejection (meas):       36.0 dB
Isolation (meas):       43.1 dB
Q Factor (meas):        11266
Group Delay Variation:  4.0 ns
Power Handling:         +33 dBm
Die Yield:              96.9%

Result Classification:  CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Band-Pass Filter design demonstrated acceptable performance for Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD).
b) Insertion loss is marginally above target; electrode thickness optimization recommended.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Slight frequency drift observed at +85°C; TC layer thickness may need adjustment.
e) ESD robustness exceeded specification by 2x margin.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
